principle: Not a coating process but the gate every coating process in this vertical must pass BEFORE product release — the owner explicitly demanded 'output test results before doing the [production/sale]'. Mechanism: each failure mode of a plated part maps to a specific measurable — thickness (wear life, label legality), adhesion (delamination), porosity (galvanic pore corrosion of the steel core, which gold ACCELERATES because Au is cathodic to steel [FACT: mechanism]), wear resistance (scratch/premium-look claim), corrosion resistance (service life), purity/karat (marketing claim legality), and nickel release (EU skin-contact legality). A small shop runs cheap in-house screens on every batch plus send-out lab tests once per product/process change; the in-house screen catches process drift, the send-out test anchors legal claims.

substrates: any plated part from the sibling process files: Au on Ni on steel wire (anchor), Au on brass/copper, PVD Au/TiN on steel or glass, electroless/immersion gold, brush-plated repairs
glass/non-conductive PVD parts (adds tape-adhesion emphasis, no ferroxyl)
applicability.steel_wire_notes: Steel core makes porosity testing NON-OPTIONAL: any pore through Au+Ni becomes a corrosion cell where the noble gold cathode drives fast rust at the pore [FACT: mechanism]. Ferroxyl test (blue-spot Fe detection) is the perfect cheap DIY porosity screen precisely BECAUSE the substrate is iron. Wire geometry also makes the mandrel wrap/bend test trivial to run — plated wire offcuts are free adhesion coupons. Curvature of thin wire degrades XRF accuracy (spot larger than flat zone): use small-spot collimation or flat coupon witnesses plated alongside.
applicability.non_conductive_notes: Glass/ceramic PVD parts: skip ferroxyl and coulometric (no conductive substrate path); rely on XRF or stylus/step profilometry for thickness, cross-hatch tape (ASTM B571/D3359 class) for adhesion, and boil/thermal-cycle test for adhesion durability. Houseware with food contact: none of the jewelry tests substitute for food-contact migration compliance [UNKNOWN — needs market-specific food-contact regulation check; jewelry-grade Ni undercoat + Co-hardened Au is NOT presumed food-safe].
applicability.jewelry_thickness_classes: LABEL-CONSTRAINT LADDER (US FTC Jewelry Guides class + trade usage) [FACT: published class structure]: 'gold flashed'/'gold washed' < 0.175 um; 'gold electroplate(d)' >= 0.175 um (7 millionths inch) of >=10k fineness gold; 'heavy gold electroplate' >= 2.5 um (100 millionths inch); 'vermeil' = STERLING SILVER base + >= 2.5 um gold (steel-core product can never be called vermeil, whatever the thickness [FACT]); 'gold filled/rolled gold plate' = mechanically clad 1/20 by weight class, not achievable by plating. ISO 27874 defines gold and gold-alloy coating classes for jewellery incl. thickness grades and fineness [FACT: standard exists]. Practical wear guidance: flash <0.2 um = days-weeks of skin wear; 0.5-1 um = light wear; 2.5-5 um = ring/bracelet class. EVERY marketing word on the label is therefore an XRF acceptance number.

components.name: XRF spectrometer (benchtop or handheld, energy-dispersive)
components.purpose: non-destructive thickness of Au (and Ni underlayer) per ISO 3497 / ASTM B568 class, plus alloy/karat composition in assay mode
components.diy_notes: the single most valuable QC asset; buying one is a significant capex — a per-sample XRF service (refiners, plating suppliers, pawn/assay offices offer it) is the correct start; needs certified thickness calibration foils (Au-on-Ni-on-Fe standards) matching YOUR stack; small-spot collimator for wire.

components.name: coulometric thickness tester (anodic dissolution)
components.purpose: destructive spot thickness per ISO 2177 / ASTM B504 class: gasketed cell dissolves the coating at constant current, endpoint = potential jump at the underlayer; Faraday's law converts charge to thickness
components.diy_notes: far cheaper than XRF, accurate on thin Au, standard in small plating shops; consumes proprietary stripping electrolytes per coating/substrate pair; leaves a small stripped spot — use on witness coupons or hidden areas.

components.name: mandrel/wrap bend jig
components.purpose: adhesion by ASTM B571 class bend test: wrap plated wire 180 deg around a mandrel (own-diameter for severest), inspect for peel vs crack
components.diy_notes: free — a set of steel rods in wire diameters + loupe; the definitive plate-then-form empirical test.

components.name: pressure-sensitive tape + cross-hatch blade
components.purpose: tape adhesion test (ASTM B571 / D3359 cross-hatch class), primary adhesion screen for PVD on glass and flat houseware
components.diy_notes: use a defined tape brand consistently (test is tape-dependent); cross-hatch cutter or razor grid 1 mm spacing.

components.name: small oven + water quench bath
components.purpose: heat-quench adhesion test ASTM B571 class: heat part to substrate-appropriate temperature, quench in water; blisters/peel = adhesion failure invisible to tape
components.diy_notes: toaster-oven class with thermocouple; typical quench temperatures ~250 C class for steel-based parts [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium — B571 tabulates per substrate]; also doubles as bake for hydrogen-embrittlement relief verification.

components.name: wear tester (Taber abraser class or reciprocating rub jig)
components.purpose: quantified wear per Taber ASTM D4060 class; gold-plating trade also uses reciprocating/rotating wear testers (Bass-type wear test class for gold electrodeposits) and simple defined rub tests (eraser/cloth, N cycles, fixed load)
components.diy_notes: a real Taber is overkill at DIY scale; build a fixed-load reciprocating rub jig (weighted felt/eraser, counter) and calibrate it against a retained good part — internal comparative standard beats no standard.

components.name: salt spray chamber (or send-out)
components.purpose: corrosion per ISO 9227 / ASTM B117 neutral salt spray class
components.diy_notes: DIY sealed-box misting rigs exist but are NOT standard-conformant (temperature, fallout rate, pH all controlled in the standard); use for comparative in-house screening only, send out for claimable hours.

components.name: porosity kit (ferroxyl papers / nitric vapor setup)
components.purpose: detect pores through Au(+Ni) to the steel core
components.diy_notes: ferroxyl is bench-trivial (see solutions); nitric acid VAPOR test (ASTM B735 class) needs a desiccator + conc. HNO3 and real ventilation — prefer ferroxyl at home.

components.name: stereo microscope / 10x loupe
components.purpose: 100% visual inspection, crack-vs-peel discrimination after bend, pore-spot counting
components.diy_notes: 10x jeweler's loupe minimum; USB microscope 50-200x is cheap and photographs defects for the log.

components.name: retained standards library
components.purpose: master color panel per product (Au color drifts with Co/pH before anything else fails), retained good/bad parts, first articles per batch
components.diy_notes: labeled zip bags + index; sealed from sulfur sources; this is the cheapest and highest-leverage QC instrument in the whole list.

components.name: precision balance (0.001 g class)
components.purpose: gravimetric cross-check of gold consumption per batch vs XRF thickness (mass balance catches drag-out losses and efficiency drift)
components.diy_notes: jewelry scale class; weigh wire coil before/after full stack.

components.name: QC logbook / batch record sheets
components.purpose: traceability: bath age, parameters, test results, disposition per batch — the acceptance protocol is only real if written
components.diy_notes: paper or spreadsheet; one row per batch; photos of defects attached.

operation_sequence.action: PRE-PRODUCTION QUALIFICATION (once per product/process/bath change): plate a qualification lot incl. flat witness coupons and wire offcuts alongside real parts
operation_sequence.parameters: same rack position, same bath state; coupons of the SAME stack (steel/Ni/Au)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: coupons plated separately or at different current density do not represent the parts — witness must ride with the work

operation_sequence.action: thickness: XRF at >=3 points per part incl. highest-wear and lowest-current-density zones (inside of ring, recesses); coulometric spot-check on witness coupon to cross-verify XRF calibration
operation_sequence.parameters: acceptance = declared label class, e.g. >=2.5 um Au for ring wear surfaces, Ni underlayer 2-5 um; XRF per ISO 3497/ASTM B568 class, coulometric per ISO 2177 class
operation_sequence.duration: 1-3 min per point (XRF), ~1-5 min per spot (coulometric)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: XRF calibrated on wrong stack reads garbage (Au-on-brass standard used for Au-on-Ni-on-steel); curvature error on thin wire; low-CD recesses can be at HALF the average thickness — measure them, not just proud surfaces

operation_sequence.action: adhesion battery on witness wire/coupons: (a) 180-deg wrap over own-diameter mandrel, (b) tape over cross-hatch, (c) heat-quench sample
operation_sequence.parameters: ASTM B571 class methods; heat-quench at substrate-appropriate temperature (~250 C class for steel [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]) then immediate water quench
operation_sequence.failure_watch: DISTINGUISH: hairline cracking of hard gold at the bend = cohesive, expected, not an adhesion reject; lifted flakes/peel exposing Ni or steel = adhesive failure = reject the batch and audit the prep chain

operation_sequence.action: porosity: ferroxyl paper test on parts sample (or nitric-vapor ASTM B735 class on coupons if equipped)
operation_sequence.parameters: ferroxyl paper pressed on surface 1-10 min class; count blue spots per cm2
operation_sequence.failure_watch: blue spots = through-pores to iron; porosity rises steeply below ~1-2 um total noble coating [FACT: published characteristic]; a 'passing thin flash' on steel is a corrosion time-bomb even when it looks perfect

operation_sequence.action: corrosion screen: artificial-sweat soak or damp-warm cabinet in-house; salt spray (ISO 9227 class) and EN 1811 nickel release as SEND-OUT tests before first sale in regulated markets
operation_sequence.parameters: in-house: 24-96 h artificial sweat at ~30-40 C class; send-out: hours per agreed class, EN 1811 with EN 12472 wear simulation for coated articles [FACT: regulation structure]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: red rust points = porosity/thickness failure; green/dark corrosion = Cu/Ni attack under thin gold; EN 1811 limits 0.5 ug/cm2/week (0.2 piercing) are pass/fail law in the EU, not a marketing option [FACT: regulation]

operation_sequence.action: wear/scratch: fixed-load rub test N cycles vs retained standard; pencil-hardness class scratch screen; Taber/Bass-class send-out only if making quantified durability claims
operation_sequence.parameters: in-house jig: define load, media, cycle count once and never change them; acceptance = no base-metal exposure at agreed cycles
operation_sequence.failure_watch: changing tape/eraser/cloth brand silently changes the test; comparative testing only works against retained standards

operation_sequence.action: purity/karat verification of the deposit: XRF assay mode on thick witness deposit (>= several um so substrate does not bleed into reading); classify vs ASTM B488 Type I (99.7 min)/II (99.0)/III (99.9) class
operation_sequence.parameters: XRF assay; fire assay (cupellation, ISO 11426 class) only via refiner for arbitration; touchstone karat acids are for bulk gold, nearly useless on thin plate (cut-through)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: XRF on <1 um Au reads the Ni/steel below and UNDER-reports gold content — thin-coating karat claims need the thick-witness method or coulometric+mass-balance

operation_sequence.action: PER-BATCH ROUTINE (after qualification passes): 100% visual at 10x; XRF first-article + sampling (e.g. sqrt(N)+1 or fixed AQL class per ISO 2859 sampling structure); one wrap-bend witness; ferroxyl spot-check; color vs master panel
operation_sequence.parameters: batch record row filled BEFORE parts move to stock
operation_sequence.failure_watch: color drift vs master panel is the EARLIEST drift alarm (Co/pH moving) — it precedes thickness/adhesion failures by many batches; skipping the batch record converts every later customer complaint into an unsolvable mystery

operation_sequence.action: disposition: accept / rework (strip and replate — gold strippers exist, value recoverable) / reject-to-refiner; retain one accepted part per batch
operation_sequence.failure_watch: shipping 'borderline' batches to test the market = brand suicide in jewelry; the retained part is your defense and your drift baseline

composition.chemical: agar or gelatin (optional, for gel/paper application)
composition.role: immobilizes reagent on the part surface (soaked paper works too)

operating_window.agitation: n/a; press soaked paper onto surface
operating_window.deposition_rate: read blue spots after 1-10 min contact

solutions.maintenance: make fresh in small batches (indicator degrades in light); store dark; dispose diluted, never into acid waste

solutions.solution_name: neutral salt spray electrolyte (ISO 9227 / ASTM B117 NSS class)
solutions.purpose: standardized accelerated corrosion exposure — the claimable corrosion test class

operating_window.agitation: continuous atomized fog, specified fallout collection rate per standard
operating_window.deposition_rate: exposure in hours: decorative classes commonly 24-96 h class; acceptance = no base-metal corrosion products

solutions.maintenance: chamber conformity (fallout rate, T, pH) is what makes results claimable — hence send-out for anything printed on a label; in-house DIY fog box = comparative screening only

solutions.purpose: in-house service-condition screen for skin-contact corrosion and the matrix for nickel-release compliance testing

solutions.maintenance: make fresh per test; EXACT recipe and analytic quantification (ICP for Ni) belong to an accredited lab — in-house version is a screen, the accredited EN 1811 result is the legal document

solutions.purpose: anodic-dissolution thickness measurement (ISO 2177 / ASTM B504 class): one electrolyte per coating/substrate pair (Au-on-Ni, Ni-on-steel)

composition.chemical: proprietary per instrument maker (Au strip solutions are commonly cyanide- or thiourea-based classes)
composition.role: selective anodic dissolution of the target layer with sharp potential endpoint
composition.hazard_class: cyanide-based variants: acutely toxic, acid-contact HCN risk [FACT for the class]; exact SDS [UNKNOWN — needs supplier SDS]

operating_window.deposition_rate: measures ~0.05-50 um class layers in 1-5 min per spot

solutions.maintenance: replace electrolyte per shot-count in TDS; cyanide-class strip solutions follow the same storage/segregation rules as plating cyanides

solutions.solution_name: nitric acid vapor porosity reagent (ASTM B735 class) — OPTIONAL, ventilated setups only
solutions.purpose: standardized porosity test for Au over Ni: acid vapor attacks Ni at pores, corrosion product spots mark pores

composition.typical_range: used neat as vapor source in closed chamber (desiccator)
composition.hazard_class: strongly corrosive, oxidizer, NOx toxic fumes [FACT]

operating_window.temperature_C: room temp, humidity-controlled chamber per standard
operating_window.agitation: none; static vapor exposure ~60 min class [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]
operating_window.deposition_rate: read pore spots at 10x after exposure

solutions.maintenance: fume-hood only; ferroxyl replaces it adequately at DIY scale on steel-core parts

prep_chain_required: 1. Witness coupons/wire offcuts plated WITH every qualification lot — WHY: destructive tests (bend, coulometric, heat-quench, nitric vapor) must not consume sellable parts, and only ride-along witnesses represent the true bath/rack condition.
2. Parts cleaned and fully dry, >=24 h after plating for corrosion/porosity tests — WHY: trapped rinse water and fresh unaged deposits give false porosity/corrosion positives.
3. XRF calibration standards matching the exact stack (Au/Ni/Fe) verified before measuring — WHY: wrong-stack calibration is the #1 source of confidently-wrong thickness numbers.
4. Written acceptance criteria per product BEFORE testing (thickness class, pore count, bend class, color tolerance) — WHY: criteria invented after seeing results always pass.
5. Retained master color panel and retained parts library established at qualification — WHY: all comparative in-house tests are anchored to them.

deposit_properties.purity_karat: What this file VERIFIES rather than produces: deposit fineness vs claim — ASTM B488 Type I 99.7/II 99.0/III 99.9 wt% Au classes for electrodeposits; FTC requires >=10k (41.7%) fineness for any 'gold plated' label [FACT: published class structure]; measure by XRF assay on >= several-um witness (thin coatings under-read).
deposit_properties.hardness_HV: verification classes: soft gold 60-90 HV, hard (Co/Ni) gold 130-200 HV/HK (ASTM B578 Knoop microindentation class on coupons) [FACT: published typical range]; DIY proxy = pencil-hardness/rub comparison vs retained standards.
deposit_properties.thickness_per_pass: n/a — acceptance thresholds instead: label ladder 0.175 um (electroplate) / 2.5 um (heavy plate, vermeil-class, ring-wear class) / 2-5 um Ni underlayer; porosity acceptable typically only above ~1-2 um total noble metal on steel [FACT/ESTIMATE mix as tagged in applicability].
deposit_properties.color_control: acceptance by comparison: master panel per product + NIHS 1N/2N/3N color-class naming [FACT: class names]; spectrophotometer CIELAB delta-E tolerance if instrumented (agree a tolerance internally; no universal jewelry delta-E law).
deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes: THE PLATE-THEN-FORM QUESTION IS SETTLED EMPIRICALLY HERE: the ASTM B571-class wrap test on plated wire IS the direct experiment — wrap plated wire around its own diameter and inspect at 10x. Expected physics: hard (Co/Ni) gold microcracks at any tight bend (elongation <1% class), soft gold + sulfamate-Ni stacks survive gentle forming [FACT: published characteristic]. Decision rule for the owner: if the wrap-test radius your ring design needs shows ANY flaking or exposes Ni/steel, the flow must be form-first-plate-second. Run this one test before buying anything else — it is free and answers Q3/Q5 of the brief.

testing_acceptance.standard_class: XRF: ISO 3497 / ASTM B568 class; coulometric: ISO 2177 / ASTM B504 class; microsection arbitration: ISO 1463 class
testing_acceptance.acceptance: >= declared label class at worst-case point (recess/inside of ring), not the average; Ni underlayer within 2-5 um window

testing_acceptance.standard_class: ASTM B571 class battery: bend/wrap, cross-hatch tape, heat-quench, burnish
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no adhesive peel/flake in any method; cohesive hairline cracks in hard gold at severe bends noted but not an adhesion reject

testing_acceptance.standard_class: ferroxyl (Fe-indicator) in-house; ASTM B735 nitric vapor / B799 SO2 classes formal
testing_acceptance.acceptance: pore count per cm2 within agreed class for the thickness sold; zero visible blue spots on ring wear surfaces at 2.5 um class

testing_acceptance.standard_class: ISO 9227/ASTM B117 NSS class (send-out for claims); artificial sweat soak in-house
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no red rust or base-metal corrosion product at agreed hours (decorative 24-96 h class); no visible tarnish/color change in 96 h sweat soak

testing_acceptance.test: nickel release (EU skin-contact, MANDATORY where sold)
testing_acceptance.standard_class: EN 1811 with EN 12472 wear-and-corrosion simulation for coated articles [FACT: regulation]
testing_acceptance.acceptance: < 0.5 ug/cm2/week (articles in prolonged skin contact), < 0.2 ug/cm2/week (piercing posts) [FACT: regulation]; accredited-lab certificate retained

testing_acceptance.standard_class: Taber ASTM D4060 class / reciprocating (Bass-type) gold-wear class / defined in-house rub test
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no base-metal exposure at agreed cycles vs retained standard; hard-gold parts must beat soft-gold reference visibly

testing_acceptance.standard_class: XRF assay on thick witness; fire assay ISO 11426 class via refiner for arbitration
testing_acceptance.acceptance: meets claimed fineness class (ASTM B488 type / >=10k FTC floor)

testing_acceptance.standard_class: visual vs retained master panel at defined light; NIHS 1N-3N naming; optional CIELAB delta-E
testing_acceptance.acceptance: within agreed tolerance vs master; drift triggers bath analysis even when parts still 'pass'

testing_acceptance.test: hydrogen embrittlement (spring-steel wire, if pickled/electrocleaned cathodically)
testing_acceptance.standard_class: post-plate bake 190-220 C class within hours of plating + sustained-bend witness [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no delayed cracking of stressed witness wire after 48 h

testing_acceptance.standard_class: FTC Jewelry Guides class (US) / ISO 27874 class / national hallmarking rules [FACT: frameworks exist; details per market UNKNOWN — needs market check]
testing_acceptance.acceptance: wording matches measured thickness+fineness ladder; 'vermeil' never used on steel-core product

defects_and_remedies.cause: calibration standard stack mismatch (Au-on-brass std for Au-on-Ni-on-steel part), curvature/spot-size error on thin wire, coating thinner than XRF info depth confounding with Ni
defects_and_remedies.remedy: buy/borrow correct-stack calibration foils; use small-spot collimation or flat ride-along coupons; cross-check with coulometric on the witness

defects_and_remedies.defect: tape test passes but parts peel in service
defects_and_remedies.cause: tape test is the WEAKEST adhesion probe — only catches gross failure; bend/heat-quench stress the interface far harder
defects_and_remedies.remedy: never release on tape alone; wrap-bend + heat-quench in the qualification battery

defects_and_remedies.defect: bend test 'failures' that are actually fine
defects_and_remedies.cause: cohesive microcracking of hard gold misread as adhesion failure
defects_and_remedies.remedy: 10x inspection: cracks with NO lifting = cohesive (expected for hard gold at tight radii); flakes/lifting = true reject; document with USB-microscope photos in the log

defects_and_remedies.defect: salt-spray hours quoted from a DIY fog box
defects_and_remedies.cause: non-conformant chamber (T, fallout, pH uncontrolled) — results are not comparable to the standard class
defects_and_remedies.remedy: in-house box = comparative screen ONLY; label-facing claims from an accredited chamber

defects_and_remedies.defect: porosity test clean, parts rust in weeks anyway
defects_and_remedies.cause: tested too soon after plating (pores plugged with rinse residue), tested proud surfaces only, or wear opened new pores in service
defects_and_remedies.remedy: test >=24 h after plating on worst-case zones; add EN 12472-class simulated wear BEFORE porosity/corrosion test for wear items

defects_and_remedies.defect: karat claim fails at a buyer's assay
defects_and_remedies.cause: XRF assay taken through <1 um gold read the Ni/steel beneath and the shop 'corrected' optimistically
defects_and_remedies.remedy: assay only on >= several-um witness deposits; keep the accredited XRF/fire-assay certificate for the deposit chemistry, re-verify after any bath change

defects_and_remedies.defect: color drift accepted for weeks, then a whole batch rejected for thickness/adhesion
defects_and_remedies.cause: color is the leading indicator of Co/pH drift; ignoring it wastes the early warning
defects_and_remedies.remedy: master-panel color check EVERY batch, with a written trigger: 'visible drift = bath analysis before next batch'

defects_and_remedies.defect: batch traceability collapse (which bath state made the returned part?)
defects_and_remedies.cause: no batch records / no retained parts
defects_and_remedies.remedy: one logbook row + one retained part per batch, no exceptions — costs minutes, saves the business during the first quality crisis

defects_and_remedies.defect: spring-steel wire snaps days after plating
defects_and_remedies.cause: hydrogen embrittlement from cathodic cleaning/pickling, no relief bake
defects_and_remedies.remedy: bake 190-220 C class within hours of plating [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]; keep stressed witness wires 48 h before batch release

cost_drivers: XRF access: benchtop/handheld purchase is the largest single QC capex vs pay-per-sample service (start with service, buy when volume justifies)
coulometric tester + per-layer electrolytes: the affordable in-house thickness anchor
accredited send-out tests: EN 1811 nickel release, conformant salt spray — per-test fees plus weeks of lead time, but they are one-time-per-product/process, not per-batch
certified XRF calibration foil sets for the exact Au/Ni/Fe stack
destructive-test material burn: witness coupons/wire, stripped spots, quenched samples — plan gold budget for QC consumption
time per batch (15-45 min routine) — the real recurring cost, and the one that gets skipped first under deadline pressure
salt spray chamber ownership only pays at real production volume; otherwise send-out
retained-standards discipline is nearly free — highest ROI item in the file

hazards: concentrated nitric acid (B735 porosity): corrosive, oxidizer, toxic NOx fumes [FACT]
potassium ferricyanide: liberates HCN on contact with strong acids or strong heating — never store or use near the pickle line [FACT]
cyanide-class coulometric strip solutions: acutely toxic class, same segregation rules as plating cyanides [FACT for the class]
ammonia and lactic acid concentrates (artificial sweat prep): corrosive/irritant [FACT]
hot oven + water quench: burn/steam hazard
salt fog: benign chemically but chamber cleaning brines are corrosive to everything nearby
controls: segregation rule mirrors the plating room: NO ferricyanide or cyanide strip solutions anywhere near acids; separate labeled shelves
nitric vapor test only with fume extraction — or simply substitute ferroxyl at DIY scale (deliberate design choice of this file)
gloves/goggles for all reagent prep; SDS binder covers TEST chemicals too, not just plating baths
small reagent volumes made fresh — QC needs milliliters, not liters; storage risk stays trivial
written test procedures so a helper cannot improvise (e.g. 'speed up' ferroxyl with acid)
safety.waste: Ferroxyl and sweat solutions: dilute, neutral, small-volume — but keep ferricyanide OUT of acid waste streams [FACT: HCN risk]. Spent nitric: neutralize/dispose as acid waste per local rules. Cyanide-class strip electrolytes: to the same licensed reclaim/disposal route as plating cyanides (they also carry dissolved gold — recoverable value). Local discharge rules [UNKNOWN — needs local regulation check].

diy_feasibility.verdict: YES — and it is the highest-leverage, lowest-cost 'process' in the whole vertical. A credible small-shop acceptance system needs almost no capex: wrap-bend jig (free), tape + cross-hatch (cheap), ferroxyl papers (cheap), artificial-sweat soak (cheap), toaster-oven heat-quench, loupe/USB microscope, logbook, retained standards. The two things that cannot be DIY'd: legally claimable numbers (EN 1811 nickel release, conformant salt spray, certified karat) = accredited send-out, once per product; and precise thickness = XRF service per sample until volume justifies a coulometric tester (first instrument to buy) and later a benchtop XRF.
diy_feasibility.minimum_viable_setup: Tier 0 (day one, ~pocket money): mandrel set, defined tape, ferroxyl reagent, sweat-soak jars, oven+quench, 10x loupe, master color panels, batch logbook, retained-parts box, 0.001 g balance. Tier 1 (first upgrade): coulometric thickness tester + Au/Ni electrolytes, USB microscope. Tier 2 (production): benchtop XRF + certified stack standards; salt-spray send-out relationship; accredited EN 1811 certificate per product line. [ESTIMATE: setup class, high confidence on tiering, no invented prices]
diy_feasibility.hard_limits: in-house results are for process control, NOT for legal claims — labels ('gold plated', thickness, karat) and EU market access (EN 1811) require accredited measurements; DIY fog boxes never equal ISO 9227 hours; XRF without correct-stack calibration is worse than no number; and no test regime rescues a product whose flow ignores the form-first-then-plate physics — the wrap test will keep saying no
